disagreements.their_reason: The scope requires byte-identical artifacts, thereby excluding the only falsifier: an append that changes a fitted artifact.
A fitted artifact changing during this update would defeat the claim that the store itself learned; fingerprints from a separate experiment do not rule that out.
A matched comparison controlling rewrite success could show no downstream-edge benefit; differing edit and ambiguity counts leave that falsifier open.
Another path-planning formulation could reach 0.912 on the same pairs; comparison against one 0.534 planner does not rule that out.
On identical three-hop questions, zero-shot accuracy could trail trained accuracy by over 0.15; the reported conditions use different sample populations and sizes.
A representation could improve generalisation without sacrificing precision on a controlled common corpus; the cross-experiment pattern does not rule this out.
The gap could plateau above zero beyond ten aliases, indicating permanent information loss; the finite shrinking curve cannot exclude that falsifier.

0.reason: The scope requires byte-identical artifacts, thereby excluding the only falsifier: an append that changes a fitted artifact.

1.reason: The falsifiers were entity penalty exceeding relation penalty or depth-2 penalty below 0.10; the measured penalties rule both out.

2.reason: A fitted artifact changing during this update would defeat the claim that the store itself learned; fingerprints from a separate experiment do not rule that out.

3.reason: The concrete falsifier was staleness exceeding refusal or wrong-answering; 1 stale case versus 150 refusals and 82 other answers rules it out.

4.reason: A matched comparison controlling rewrite success could show no downstream-edge benefit; differing edit and ambiguity counts leave that falsifier open.

5.reason: A depth-2 held-out/trained gap over 0.02 would falsify parity; the observed gap is 0.011.

6.reason: Another path-planning formulation could reach 0.912 on the same pairs; comparison against one 0.534 planner does not rule that out.

7.reason: On identical three-hop questions, zero-shot accuracy could trail trained accuracy by over 0.15; the reported conditions use different sample populations and sizes.

8.reason: Fewer than 5821 refusals on the specified sparse chain-break population would falsify the claim; the direct count rules that out.

9.reason: Failure to raise not-applicable refusal or reduce answerable wrongness would falsify it; both paired measurements move as claimed.

10.reason: A nonnegative branching-refusal correlation in any stated population would falsify the descriptive claim; all three measured correlations are strongly negative.

11.reason: A representation could improve generalisation without sacrificing precision on a controlled common corpus; the cross-experiment pattern does not rule this out.

12.reason: The gap could plateau above zero beyond ten aliases, indicating permanent information loss; the finite shrinking curve cannot exclude that falsifier.

13.reason: A head gap above 0.05 in any specified population would falsify 'free'; all three gaps remain below that threshold while retrieval drops sharply.
